name: Stop the Bus
description: Stop the Bus is a fast-paced commerce game played with 3 cards, similar to Commerce and 31. Players start with 3 lives (tokens) and aim to *not* have the worst hand when someone calls 'Stop the Bus'. The game is elimination-based, with the last surviving player winning.

overview.description: Stop the Bus is a fast-paced commerce game played with 3 cards, similar to Commerce and 31. Players start with 3 lives (tokens) and aim to *not* have the worst hand when someone calls 'Stop the Bus'. The game is elimination-based, with the last surviving player winning.

history.origins: Stop the Bus is a British draw-and-discard game in the commerce family. It shares mechanisms with Commerce (18th century) and Thirty-One (Scat), in which players draw and discard to improve a three-card hand. The version documented here was contributed by Nic Cleveland from Guernsey; the name is also used for a Thirty-One variant (Ride the Bus) and for Bastard Brag, which uses table exchange instead of stock and discard.
timeline: 2000s: Popular as a quick pub game.
2010s: Online apps bring it to a wider audience.
history.cultural: A game of nerve: calling 'Stop' forces everyone to reveal.
history.evolution: The 'Bus' theme is purely thematic (last bus home? losing your ride?).

setup.players: From two to around nine or more can play; the game is best with three to five. With more players, those eliminated early have nothing to do until the game ends.
setup.deck: A standard Anglo-American 52-card pack; cards in each suit rank high to low A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2.
setup.dealing: Dealer shuffles and deals three cards to each player one at a time face down. The next card is placed face up to start the discard pile; the remainder is placed face down as the stock.
setup.equipment: Three tokens (e.g. pennies or matches) per player; optionally a small model bus to signal end of play.

rules.objective: Form the best three-card Brag hand. Do not have the worst hand when someone calls Stop the Bus; the lowest hand loses a life.
rules.gameplay: Dealer deals three cards each and turns one card face up to start the discard pile; the rest form the stock. Player to dealer's left starts; play is clockwise. On your turn you may: (1) Draw the top card of the stock (face down), add it to your hand, then discard one of your four cards face up onto the discard pile; (2) Draw the top card of the discard pile, add it to your hand, then discard a different card from your hand face up; or (3) Call 'Stop the Bus' and keep your current three cards without drawing or discarding. When someone calls Stop the Bus, each other player has one more turn (they may pass without drawing). All then show hands; the player with the worst Brag hand loses one life (token). A player with no tokens left is eliminated. Play continues with new deals until one player remains.
keyRules: Hands are ranked by three-card Brag order: Prial (three of a kind) best, then Running Flush, Run, Flush, Pair, High Card.
Tiebreak: compare suit of highest card using spades > hearts > diamonds > clubs.
If the player due to deal next was eliminated, the same dealer deals again so the next surviving player to the left does not miss their turn to start.

strategy.basic: Go for 31 (Ace-Ten-Face same suit). Or 3 of a kind (30). Don't hold disparate suits. Watch what opponents pick up. If they take a 10 of Hearts, assume they have Hearts.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Stop' Bluff: Call 'Stop' early with a decent hand (e.g., 20 points) if you think someone else has garbage. It forces them to panic.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Swapping: Pick up a high card just to deny it to the next player, even if it doesn't help you much (as long as it doesn't ruin your hand).
tips: Don't get stuck with a 3-card rainbow.

variations.name: Bastard Stop the Bus
variations.description: Variant where players exchange cards with a 3-card hand on the table rather than drawing and discarding from stock/discard. Same Brag hand ranking and elimination by lives.
